import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from brackets.core import is_balanced

def test():
    # Test cases from acceptance criteria
    assert is_balanced('') == True
    assert is_balanced('()') == True
    assert is_balanced('[]') == True
    assert is_balanced('{}') == True
    assert is_balanced('()[]{}') == True
    assert is_balanced('([{}])') == True
    assert is_balanced('(a[b]{c})') == True
    assert is_balanced('f(x[0], y[1])') == True
    assert is_balanced('(') == False
    assert is_balanced(')') == False
    assert is_balanced('([)]') == False
    assert is_balanced('(]') == False
    assert is_balanced('{[}') == False
    assert is_balanced('())') == False
    # Additional edge cases
    assert is_balanced('([)]') == False  # already
    assert is_balanced('({[]})') == True
    assert is_balanced('({[}])') == False
    # Non-bracket characters ignored
    assert is_balanced('abc') == True
    assert is_balanced('a(b)c[d]e{f}g') == True
    assert is_balanced('a(b]c') == False
    # Type checking
    try:
        is_balanced(None)
        assert False, "Expected TypeError"
    except TypeError:
        pass
    try:
        is_balanced(123)
        assert False, "Expected TypeError"
    except TypeError:
        pass
    try:
        is_balanced([''])
        assert False, "Expected TypeError"
    except TypeError:
        pass
    # Ensure return type is bool
    assert isinstance(is_balanced(''), bool)
    assert isinstance(is_balanced('('), bool)
    print('All tests passed')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test()
